data.contract: Read-only detail from the existing twelve runs; no new performance samples or censoring. Callbacks and top requests use complete planned-arrival cohort records, including late finishes. Threshold wait_ms sums full waits of callbacks strictly above each threshold; thresholds are nested. All timestamps are relative to each run origin. source is the submission-context pool, chosen is actual placement; no inferred preferred-pool column. Same-pool overlap includes all recorded requests and counts callback execution wall intervals, not on-CPU/runnable time or causally attributed delay. Sum of overlapping callback wall time can exceed the wait; union cannot. Callback cpu_ms is the existing callback CPU measurement, not CPU time inside its waiting interval. No critical-path or summed-wait latency decomposition.

limitations: Offline detail from the same twelve 4027 runs, not additional trials.
Original target CSVs are not available locally; their reported hashes match 4027.
Callback-wall coverage is neither CPU usage nor kernel runnable/queue state.
Post-parent bound uses this synchronous DAG: child submitted within parent callback, parent wall <= cohort max wall; parent finish follows child add return.
Each max term is a different run order statistic, not matched-request causal cost.
All 192 requests remain in the primary mean; other term is not a new mean over 191 requests.
No exclusion/censoring, warmup change, workload or policy change.
